findings.message: The hasRepoScript fallback in handleGitUpdate cannot fire for global installs: classifyInstallPath returns npm-global/pnpm-global for any /node_modules/ path, so those never reach it. It only fires for source checkouts, where it offers `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`. That leaves the checkout un-updated and installs a second global copy that may shadow the npm-linked ao. A rebuild hint is the correct action.
The 'script unavailable' fallback test mocks detectInstallMethod as 'git', so it locks in the source-checkout → npm install -g behaviour rather than testing the global-install scenario from #1252.

The default REPO_ROOT ($(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/..) now resolves to .../assets after the move. Run directly without AO_REPO_ROOT, the root is wrong and layout detection can never pick package-install (same in ao-update.sh line 43).
The 'bundled doctor script is available' check is self-referential and always passes in practice.
The regex-escape pattern /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g is malformed and escapes nothing. The test passes only because an unescaped '.' acts as a wildcard.

The fallback only runs when the install is classified 'git', never for the global npm/pnpm installs of #1252. Where it does fire, it offers npm install -g and reports 'Update complete', replacing the earlier clear 'Script not found' error with a misleading action that never updates the checkout.
The test forces detectInstallMethod=git with hasRepoScript=false. It locks in the questionable fallback and never exercises a real global-install path, though its name suggests #1252 coverage.

Dropping the scripts/ao-update.sh guard means any non-node_modules location with .git four levels up counts as 'git' (e.g. vendored inside another repo). The 'unknown' test was deleted with no replacement guard.
The fix relies on CLI_DIST_ROOT resolving to dist/ in a packaged install, but no test checks it. hasRepoScript is mocked in every caller test.
Script cwd silently changed from the repo root to process.cwd(). ao-doctor.sh walks up from $PWD to find config, so git installs now find config from the user's directory.
The REPO_ROOT fallback resolves to src/assets after the move (same in ao-update.sh line 43). Direct invocation without AO_REPO_ROOT uses the wrong root, and the update script's smoke-test paths fail.
The packaged-install test sets AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT explicitly, so the script's own layout detection goes untested. The fake dist/index.js makes the runtime sanity check pass regardless.
The 'bundled doctor script is available' check is self-referential and can only pass in normal use.

The escape regex closes its character class early and never escapes anything. A checkout path containing +, ( or [ would break the test; use /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g correctly as /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g → /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/ fixed to /[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g with the class written [.*+?^${}()|[\]\\].

When detection says git but ao-update.sh is missing, this branch hard-codes the npm-global command and can install a global copy that shadows the npm link launcher. It is nearly unreachable; a rebuild hint would be more accurate.
Install detection returns 'git' whenever .git exists four levels up, with no second signal. Checking for packages/cli/package.json under that root would restore one.
The REPO_ROOT fallback was not updated after the move and resolves to .../assets (same in ao-update.sh line 43). Direct runs fall into the source-checkout branch and fail its checks.
hasRepoScript now checks bundled assets, not repo scripts. hasBundledScript would fit.
The scripts' cwd changed from the repo root to the caller's cwd. ao-update.sh cd's itself, but the doctor now searches for config from the user's cwd, an undocumented behaviour change.

AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT is passed from TS while ao-doctor.sh also re-derives the layout by sniffing files: two detection mechanisms for one fact. resolveScriptLayout's override branch exists only for the env var.
resolveScriptLayoutFromPath and resolveDefaultRepoRootFromPath are exported only for tests and are '/node_modules/' substring heuristics.
The error message repeats the scripts directory inside 'Expected at' and in the parenthetical. Dropping the parenthetical also removes the test's regex escaping.

The fallback adds an optional fallbackMethod parameter that hard-codes 'npm-global', ignoring what detection found. It is near-dead code, since checkouts always have the script and package installs classify as npm.

The package-install branch checks dist/index.js in both check_install_layout and check_runtime_sanity, reporting the same failure twice. Checking for its own scripts in dist/assets is self-referential.
Dropping the scripts/ao-update.sh existence check is an acceptable simplification.
The fallback always uses getUpdateCommand('npm-global'), so pnpm/yarn users are told the wrong command. The 'package-manager update flow' message is generic.
classifyInstallPath no longer requires scripts/ao-update.sh, so any .git at the guessed root counts as a git install, removing a guard against false positives.
The default REPO_ROOT is wrong now that the script sits in assets/scripts. It is only reached on manual runs without AO_REPO_ROOT.
Layout detection by '/node_modules/' substring treats tarball or linked installs outside node_modules as source checkouts, and the runner's value always overrides doctor's own guess.
